newsitem.title: GERMANY: German labour office - economy not creating jobs.
newsitem.headline: German labour office - economy not creating jobs.

text.p: The head of Germany's Federal Labour Office said on Tuesday that the economy remained too weak to bring much relief to the beleaguered jobs market.
"Economic growth in the german economy is too weak to encourage an increase in the number of jobs," Bernhard Jagoda told a news conference in Nurmeberg.
Fresh labour market data showed a rise in pan-German seasonally adjusted unemployment in April to 4.299 million.
"Looking at the development since January, we can see a flattening out of the growth in unemployed, at least in west Germany," Jagoda said.
However, this was not the case in the former east Germany.

"In the eastern German states the rise in seasonally adjusted unemployment continues unabated; there the average rose 18,000 (per month since January) which is just as strong as in the last four months of last year," he added.
